ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word rhymes with 'road'? (1 mark)
   A. lead
   B. load
   C. rod
   D. raid

2. What is the plural of 'tooth'? (1 mark)
   A. tooths
   B. teeths
   C. teeth
   D. toothes

3. Which is a greeting for the afternoon? (1 mark)
   A. Good night
   B. Good afternoon
   C. Good luck
   D. Good morning

4. Which letter is a tall letter? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. e
   C. h
   D. n

5. Which is an object pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. his
   B. him
   C. he
   D. I

6. Narratives: Which sentence has a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The bread was soft.
   B. We ate bread.
   C. Bread is food.
   D. The bread was as soft as a pillow.

7. Intonation is (1 mark)
   A. the spelling of a word
   B. the rise and fall of the voice
   C. the length of a word
   D. a kind of computer

8. Which sentence usually ends with a falling voice? (1 mark)
   A. Can I use it?
   B. Is the file here?
   C. Did you send it?
   D. Where is the file?

9. In a written dialogue, the speaker's name is usually followed by (1 mark)
   A. a colon
   B. nothing
   C. a full stop only
   D. a bracket

10. A pictorial composition is (1 mark)
   A. a story written from a set of pictures
   B. a song
   C. a map
   D. a shopping list

11. Which is a good listening habit? (1 mark)
   A. Look at the speaker
   B. Look out of the window
   C. Talk to your neighbour
   D. Shout answers before the question ends

12. Which is the best thing to do if an online message makes you afraid? (1 mark)
   A. Reply to the stranger
   B. Show it to a trusted adult at once
   C. Send it to all your friends
   D. Keep it a secret

13. Choose the correct -ing form of 'lie' (to rest flat). (1 mark)
   A. lieing
   B. lying
   C. lyeing
   D. liing

14. What is the negative form of 'We are shouting'? (1 mark)
   A. We are no shouting.
   B. We not are shouting.
   C. We do not shouting.
   D. We are not shouting.

15. What is an abbreviation? (1 mark)
   A. A short way of writing a word or group of words
   B. A type of story
   C. A kind of question
   D. A long sentence

16. Which of these does NOT need a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Eid
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. dry season
   D. Christmas

17. Which is NOT one of the three parts of reading fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Expression
   B. Speed
   C. Accuracy
   D. Handwriting

18. Why is fast reading not always good reading? (1 mark)
   A. Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   B. Fast readers cannot use their eyes
   C. Speed is never important
   D. Books are meant to be read slowly only

19. Which of these is a nonverbal cue that shows confidence? (1 mark)
   A. Standing straight and looking at your audience
   B. Turning your back
   C. Hiding your face
   D. Looking at the floor

20. Which adverb of frequency completes: 'I ____ wash my hands before eating.' (every time)? (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. rarely
   C. always
   D. seldom

21. Which adverb has the same form as its adjective? (1 mark)
   A. slowly
   B. gently
   C. quickly
   D. hard

22. Which conjunction gives a choice? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. so
   C. yet
   D. and

23. In which tense is a description usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Future perfect
   B. Command form
   C. Present tense
   D. Past perfect

24. Which sentence uses the sense of touch? (1 mark)
   A. The room is bright.
   B. We heard laughter.
   C. The soup tasted sweet.
   D. The towel is soft and dry.

25. Which is a fact that can be checked? (1 mark)
   A. Netball is boring.
   B. Everyone should play netball.
   C. A netball team has seven players.
   D. Netball is the nicest game.

26. What is a digital text? (1 mark)
   A. A spoken poem
   B. A hand-written letter
   C. A text printed on paper only
   D. A text read on a screen

27. Which day is spelt correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Wenesday
   B. Wednesday
   C. Wednsday
   D. Wensday

28. Which word begins with the cluster 'gr'? (1 mark)
   A. swim
   B. clap
   C. glass
   D. grass

29. What is hesitation in speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Using gestures
   B. Stopping or saying 'um' and 'er'
   C. Speaking clearly
   D. Speaking loudly

30. Which time word often goes with the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. yesterday
   B. already
   C. in 2010
   D. last week

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the past participle of: write, see, take. (3 marks)

32. Name two things that a good listener does when a story is read aloud. (2 marks)

33. Explain the difference between 'my' and 'mine'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

34. Write a polite request to borrow a ruler from a classmate. (2 marks)

35. Plan a composition called 'My School Compound' by saying what goes into each of three paragraphs. (3 marks)

36. Write four words with double consonants and four words with blends. (4 marks)

37. Write two polite phrases you could use in a conversation, one to add something and one to give the other person a turn. (2 marks)

38. Give two nonverbal cues that show a speaker is confident. (2 marks)

39. Name three parts of a newspaper. (3 marks)

40. Explain three uses of the comma with an example for each. (5 marks)

41. Write three tall letters and three tail letters. (3 marks)

42. Write four sentences using words with double consonants that you have learnt. (4 marks)

43. Write a short headline and two sentences for a news story about your school. (3 marks)

44. Explain how guide words help you find a word quickly. (3 marks)

45. Say whether the voice falls or rises at the end of: (a) Who sent the message? (b) Is the phone on the table? (2 marks)

46. Use the words 'sibling', 'relative' and 'chore' in three sentences about a family. (3 marks)

47. Give three questions to ask yourself when you proofread. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — load
   Road and load both end with /əʊd/.

2. C — teeth
   Tooth is irregular.

3. B — Good afternoon
   Good afternoon is used after midday.

4. C — h
   H reaches the top line.

5. B — him
   Him is the object form of he.

6. D — The bread was as soft as a pillow.
   It compares bread with a pillow using as ... as.

7. B — the rise and fall of the voice
   It is the tune of our voice.

8. D — Where is the file?
   WH questions usually fall.

9. A — a colon
   For example: Baraka: I miss Grandmother.

10. A — a story written from a set of pictures
   The pictures guide the events.

11. A — Look at the speaker
   Looking at the speaker shows you are listening.

12. B — Show it to a trusted adult at once
   A trusted adult can help you stay safe.

13. B — lying
   The letters ie change to y before -ing.

14. D — We are not shouting.
   Not comes after are.

15. A — A short way of writing a word or group of words
   For example Dr. for Doctor.

16. C — dry season
   Seasons are common nouns and take small letters.

17. D — Handwriting
   Fluency is accuracy, speed and expression.

18. A — Mistakes and lost meaning mean you must read again
   Rushing causes errors that hurt understanding.

19. A — Standing straight and looking at your audience
   Posture and eye contact show confidence.

20. C — always
   'Always' means every time.

21. D — hard
   'He works hard' uses hard as an adverb.

22. A — or
   'Or' offers choices.

23. C — Present tense
   Descriptions often say what something is like now.

24. D — The towel is soft and dry.
   'Soft and dry' describes how it feels.

25. C — A netball team has seven players.
   A fact can be checked; the others are opinions.

26. D — A text read on a screen
   Digital texts are read on phones, tablets and computers.

27. B — Wednesday
   Wednesday is spelt Wed-nes-day.

28. D — grass
   'Grass' begins with g and r.

29. B — Stopping or saying 'um' and 'er'
   Practise to hesitate less.

30. B — already
   'Already' fits the present perfect; finished-time words do not.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: written, seen, taken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker; do not interrupt; think about what you hear; ask a question when the speaker finishes (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: My comes before a noun (This is my bag). Mine stands alone (The bag is mine).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence and 1 mark for the difference.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: May I borrow your ruler, please?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for may I and 1 mark for please.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Paragraph 1: what the compound is and where. Paragraph 2: details such as trees, playground, buildings. Paragraph 3: how I feel about it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each paragraph.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Double: letter, dinner, apple, bottle. Blends: train, snake, clap, flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group of two words, up to 4.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: 'May I add something?' and 'What do you think?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable polite phrase.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Eye contact and standing straight; a smile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Masthead (name), headline, byline, article, picture, caption, advert, weather report (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: In lists: rice, beans and cabbage. After yes or no: Yes, I can. When addressing a person: Mama, come here. Also before but/so between sentences.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use and example (max 5 including quality of examples).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tall: b, d, h (or f, k, l, t). Tail: g, p, y (or j, q).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each set, up to 3, with a mark for correctness.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four correct sentences with correctly spelt double consonant words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Headline: Pupils Win Football Match. The school team won 2 to 1 on Friday. The pupils were happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a headline and 1 for each sentence.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Guide words show the first and last word on a page. If your word comes between them alphabetically, it is on that page. If not, turn forward or backward.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what guide words show, 1 mark for comparing your word, 1 mark for turning pages.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) falls (b) rises
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: My sibling is my little sister. My aunt is a relative. My chore is to sweep the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Does every sentence start with a capital letter? Are words spelt correctly? Does my story have a beginning, middle and end?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.
